If another bridge has attachments $\{b,c,d\}$, contract its interior to $v$ and an outside $c$--$e$ path to $ce$. If $cd$ is an edge, use $ce,cd$ instead. Keeping these additions and $\Psi_3\cup B$ gives
\[
H_0=(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce+v\quad\hbox{or}\quad H_0=(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce+cd.
\]
In both cases, $H_0-\operatorname{Int}(B)$ contains a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision with parts $\{a,d,e\}$ and $\{r,z,c\}$, using $cpa$, either $cd$ or $cvd$, the edge $ce$, and the edges at $r,z$. Every complementary region is therefore a disk. The facial walks containing $a,b,d$ give exactly $abad,abd,adbd$~\supp{R11}. The first and last give the tests $B+ab+ad$ and $B+ad+bd$, while $abd$ gives the triangle completion, whose planarity implies both. Corollary~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} therefore gives
\begin{equation}\label{r1:two-cap-test}
H_0\text{ is toroidal}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
B+ab+ad\text{ is planar or }B+ad+bd\text{ is planar}.
\end{equation}
Both $B+ab+ad$ and $B+ad+bd$ are nonplanar, so minimality gives $G=H_0$. If $B+ad$ is nonplanar, apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} to a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision in it. Both completions contain $B+ad$, so both remain nonplanar after this reduction. Minimality and Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} give the $563$ forms with added edge $ad$. Every resulting graph has a $K_5$ minor or a proper nontoroidal minor except four in the $cd$ case, isomorphic to $\mathfrak T_{52},\mathfrak T_{57},\mathfrak T_{58},\mathfrak T_{59}$. The first three have twin triples meeting in zero or two vertices, and the last has a choice of twins giving a component with four neighbors~\supp{E33}. Thus $B+ad$ is planar. Any proper allowed minor keeping both completions in~\eqref{r1:two-cap-test} nonplanar would contradict minimality, so Lemma~\ref{core:two-cap-critical} applies with $(x,y,z)=(a,d,b)$. Since $B+ab+bd$ is nonplanar, the $Q$ form is excluded. Hence $B$ consists of the cycle $up'u'q'u$, the edges $bu,bu'$, and either
\[
N_B(d)=\{p',q'\},\quad N_B(a)=\{u'\},
\qquad\hbox{or}\qquad
N_B(a)=\{p',q'\},\quad N_B(d)=\{u'\}.
\]
In the first case, the twin triple $\{d,u,u'\}$ is disjoint from $\{a,b,c\}$. In the second, choose the twins with neighborhood $\{a,u,u'\}$ together with $r,z$. The component outside the new $\Psi_3$ containing $b,c,p,q$ has neighbors at $u,u'$ through $b$, at $e$ through $ce$, at $d$ through $cd$ or $v$, and at $a$ through $p$. The first case contradicts the assumption that distinct twin triples meet in exactly one vertex. The second gives a component with five neighbors, although every component outside every choice of $\Psi_3$ has exactly three.

vertex names: Psi_3: twins p, q with neighbourhood {a,b,c} and r, z with neighbourhood {a,d,e}, as in Section 6. Further vertices with neighbourhood {a,b,c} are p3, p4, and with {a,d,e} r3, r4. Interior vertices of bridges are u0, u1, ...
